rows.title: Equivalent characterizations of second-countable type I groups
rows.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a second-countable locally compact group $G$ the following are equivalent: (i) $G$ is type I; (ii) every factor representation of $G$ on a separable Hilbert space is type I (equivalently, is a multiple of an irreducible); (iii) the Mackey Borel structure and the Fell-topology Borel structure on $\widehat G$ coincide and $\widehat G$ is standard Borel; (iv) $\widehat G$ is countably separated ([[def-mackey-borel-structure-and-countable-separation]]); (v) the map $\kappa:\widehat G\to\operatorname{Prim}(C^*(G))$ is a homeomorphism onto its image.
rows.strategy: Assemble the clauses of the corrected criteria lemma and the fixed definition of type-I factor/group. The criteria supplier uses exactly the authorized original Glimm implication inline and proves every remaining GCR/Borel/kernel direction locally. This theorem introduces no independent cited fact. For second-countable groups a cyclic subrepresentation of a factor has separable carrier; the criteria supplier proves the faithful normal restriction argument needed to pass between the separable-carrier convention and all factor representations. Preserve the full standard-dual, countable-separation and primitive-homeomorphism equivalences.

rows.title: Non-type-I groups have non-smooth irreducible disintegration
rows.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact group which is not of type I. Then the irreducible decomposition of representations of $G$ is not canonical in the sense of [[thm-irreducible-direct-integral-decomposition-for-type-i-groups]]: there exist a separable strongly continuous unitary representation $(\pi,H)$ and two direct integral decompositions into irreducible representations $$\pi\cong\int_X^\oplus\pi_x\,d\mu(x)\cong\int_Y^\oplus\sigma_y\,d\nu(y)$$ whose irreducible components satisfy $\pi_x\not\cong\sigma_y$ for every $(x,y)\in X\times Y$. Only the central (factor) decomposition remains canonical; the theorem does not assert that no irreducible decompositions exist.
rows.strategy:
First prove local nonsmoothness: non-type-I implies non-GCR by contraposition of the locally proved GCR-to-factor-type-I direction; the faithful-orbit category supplier gives failure of countable separation of the Mackey dual ([[def-mackey-borel-structure-and-countable-separation]]). This does NOT prove the stronger universal witness.
INLINE OWNER-AUTHORIZED ORIGINAL DIXMIER FACT: Corollaire2 of Dixmier1964 states that for a separable non-type-I C*-algebra A and every n>0, nonzero positive measures supported on pairwise disjoint standard Borel subsets of its Mackey spectrum have equivalent irreducible direct integrals. Read the actual4pages and use this exact fact under the authority; its hyperfinite-commutant/simple-MASA proof still imports the Glimm construction and is not presented as a local proof.
Take A=C*(G), which is separable by the earlier supplier and is non-type-I because the group/algebra nondegenerate correspondence preserves factor representations. Specialize the cited fact to n=2. Use the sigma-finite standard measures of its separable direct-integral construction (equivalent finite spectral measure models if necessary); choose the two disjoint standard Borel supports as X,Y. Measurable irreducible C*-representation fields give strongly continuous irreducible G fields by the established correspondence, with each g obtained as the strong limit of integrated translates of a sequential L1 approximate identity; the countable algebra field thus supplies coefficient measurability for every fixed g. The integrated algebra representations are nondegenerate by their common approximate identity and dominated convergence on the fibre field, hence they correspond to separable strongly continuous group representations. An algebra intertwiner is a group intertwiner by the correspondence; conversely a group intertwiner intertwines every integrated algebra element. Therefore the two globally equivalent algebra direct integrals yield one equivalent group representation, while any equivalence between a fibre from X and a fibre from Y would contradict their distinct original irreducible algebra classes. Disjoint supports give non-equivalence for EVERY retained cross pair; null exceptional fibres are deleted once. Central factor decomposition/uniqueness remains locally proved. The F2 B example is a separate actual local example, not a universal witness supplier. Do not claim original Glimm full-text reading or a locally supplied proof of a cited clause; do not expand the exception to another step.
